property_summary: After seeding an empty market with seedMarket, the contract becomes usable (initialized==true) so getFreeKilo succeeds and grants STARTING_KILOS to a caller with zero kilos.
After seeding an empty market, the contract must allow a caller with zero kilos to receive the STARTING_KILOS via getFreeKilo (i.e., getMyKilo() > 0), which requires the contract to be initialized.

After seeding an empty market, the contract must become initialized so that seedMarket makes the contract report initialized() == true (allowing subsequent view-observable behaviors that require initialization).
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs was zero, the contract becomes initialized=true and marketDrugs equals the supplied amount.
After seeding the market when it is empty, the contract reports initialized == true (i.e., the market becomes initialized).
After calling seedMarket(drugs) with zero ETH, the contract remains uninitialized (initialized == false).
After calling seedMarket with any drugs value when marketDrugs was previously zero, the contract becomes initialized (initialized == true).
After seeding the market (when marketDrugs was zero) the contract will report a positive marketDrugs value and the contract's initialized flag will be true regardless of any Ether sent.
After seeding an untouched market, c.initialized() must be true and marketDrugs equals the seeded amount.
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs was zero, initialized must be true (market remains seeded and contract is initialized).
If marketDrugs is zero and the caller seeds the market, afterwards the contract must be initialized (true).
If marketDrugs is zero before seeding, then after seedMarket the contract's initialized flag must be true.

After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs is zero, the contract's marketDrugs becomes equal to the supplied drugs parameter and remains nonzero (i.e., seeding sets marketDrugs to the provided positive value).

For any initial call to seedMarket when marketDrugs==0, the reference contract sets initialized to true deterministically; the mutant toggles initialized instead, so there exist inputs (an initial seedMarket call from any account) where initialized in mutant != true, violating the rule.

After seeding the market from any caller when marketDrugs==0, the reference contract always sets initialized == true; the mutant flips initialized (so for some initial states it will be false), violating this invariant.

After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs == 0, the reference contract always sets initialized == true for every caller, whereas the mutant may leave initialized != true (it toggles), so there exist callers for which initialized is false — the test asserts initialized == true after seeding.

After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs == 0, the reference contract always sets initialized() == true for every caller; the mutant toggles initialized instead, so there exist inputs where initialized() != true.

For any caller and any nonzero drugs value when marketDrugs==0, calling seedMarket(...) results in initialized == true in the reference contract; the mutant that toggles initialized can leave initialized == false for some initial states/callers, violating this property.
Only the original contract refuses to let a non-CEO overwrite ceoAddress via DrugDealer; i.e., calling DrugDealer from an address different than the current ceoAddress must not change c.ceoAddress().
Calling DrugDealer() does not change ceoAddress when msg.sender is the current ceoAddress (i.e., the current CEO can call DrugDealer without changing the CEO).

property_summary: Only the current CEO is prevented from successfully calling DrugDealer (calls by the current ceoAddress must revert).
Calls to DrugDealer by the current CEO always revert (i.e., when msg.sender equals c.ceoAddress()), the call must revert.
Only the current CEO is allowed to successfully call DrugDealer (calls by non-CEO must revert).

Only the original contract prevents changing ceoAddress when called via a contract (msg.sender != tx.origin), so calling DrugDealer through a contract should leave ceoAddress equal to the caller (msg.sender) — not to an external tx.origin.

property_summary: When DrugDealer is invoked directly by an EOA (caller equals tx.origin), the call must revert on the original but not on the mutant; equivalently, for any address invoking DrugDealer, if msg.sender == tx.origin then the original contract's DrugDealer must revert (so reverted == true).

For any caller who is the current ceoAddress, calling DrugDealer() leaves ceoAddress equal to msg.sender (i.e., CEO remains the caller); the mutant instead overwrites ceoAddress with a fixed burn address for some caller, breaking this property.

For any caller who is the current ceoAddress, after calling DrugDealer() the contract's ceoAddress remains equal to the caller (i.e., CEO can re-set themselves to their own EOA); the mutant breaks this because it sets ceoAddress to address(this) instead of msg.sender.
